attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (RHEL 9) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 so the kernel OOM killer will not select it. Verified end-to-end under a real system-wide OOM: with swap disabled, a hog process was driven to ~1.8GB RSS on a 1.9GB-RAM box; the kernel oom-killer killed the hog while inventory-api (PID 1602, unchanged) stayed active and kept answering /healthz and /inventory. Swap was restored afterward. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, issued systemctl reboot asynchronously so the exec ack returned first, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id proving an actual restart, and confirmed inventory-api auto-started (fresh PID, enabled, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact) and served correct inventory data post-reboot.
